stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. This funding will enhance their co-orbital security capabilities, a hot topic given rising geopolitical tensions in space. The Department of Defense's increasing interest in space domain awareness is driving this investment.
stories.soWhat: In an era where cash is king, True Anomaly's success underscores the DoD's shift toward prioritizing space security over traditional defense.

stories.head: GAO flags Space Force's budget mismanagement
stories.body: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) reported significant cost overruns and launch risks in the Space Force's satellite portfolio, suggesting that budget gymnastics may be overshadowing actual security needs. With $1.4 billion added to the FY27 budget for space resilience, lawmakers are finally acknowledging the financial strain.
stories.soWhat: If the Space Force can't get its budget house in order, we might find ourselves with a robust portfolio of shiny satellites that don’t actually work.

stories.head: Pegasus launches Swift, but is it the end?
stories.body: Pegasus successfully launched the Swift reboost mission, but this might also signal the twilight of a rocket that never quite captured the limelight. After years of underperformance, Pegasus's future is uncertain as the industry shifts towards more reliable launch options.
stories.soWhat: In a world where every rocket needs to justify its existence, the Pegasus might just be the first casualty of the new launch economy.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Hongqing's $191M funding
watchlist.body: With this significant investment, Hongqing is poised to challenge established satellite manufacturers, potentially shaking up the market.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser moves forward
watchlist.body: Clearing the critical design review is a milestone, but can they actually launch before the next ice age? The clock is ticking.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris bid for SDA
watchlist.body: Their collaboration could set a precedent for future defense contracts, but it also raises questions about who really benefits from shared risk.

watchlist.title: Watch for GPS jamming developments
watchlist.body: The return of GPS jamming to pre-2024 levels suggests a growing need for robust countermeasures in military operations.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
